II.}}</noinclude>thou contemne the riches of his goodnes, and patience, and longanimity, not knovving that the benignity of God bringeth thee to penance? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=5}}† But according to thy hardnes and impenitent hart, thou heapest to thy self vvrath, in the day of vvrath and of the reuelation of the iust iudgement of God, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6}}† vvho vvil {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 61, 13.''}}* render to euery man {{sup|‖}} according to his vvorkes. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Good men also according to the merits of their good vvil shal haue their reward. ''Aug. ep. 47''. · Psal. 61, 13.}}∷ to them truely that according to patience in good vvorke, seeke glorie and honour and incorruption, life eternal. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8}}† but to them that are of contention, and that obey not the truth, but giue credite to iniquitie, vvrath and indignation. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=9}}† Tribulation and anguish vpon euery soul of man that vvorketh euil, of the Ievve first and of the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ That is, the ''Gentile.''}}∷ Greeke: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=10}}† but glorie and honour and peace to euery one that vvorketh good, to the Ievv first and to the Greeke. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11}}† for {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 10, 17. Act. 10, 34.''}}* there is no acception of persons vvith God. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=12}}† For vvhosoeuer haue sinned vvithout the Lavv, vvithout the Lavv shal perish: and vvhosoeuer haue sinned in the Lavv, by the Lavv shal be iudged. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=13}}† For {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 7, 21. Ia. 1, 22.''}}* {{sup|‖}} not the hearers of the Lavv are iust vvith God: but the doers of the Lavv {{sup|‖}} shal be iustified. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=14}}† For vvhen the Gentiles vvhich haue not the Lavv, naturally doe those things that are of the Lavv: the same not hauing the Lavv, them selues are a lavv to them selues: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=15}}† vvho shevv the vvorke of the Lavv vvritten in their hartes, their conscience giuing testimonie to them, and among them selues mutually their thoughtes accusing, or also defending, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=16}}† in the day vvhen God shal iudge the secretes of men, according to my Gospel, by {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=17}}† But if thou be surnamed a Ievv, and restest in the Lavv, and doest glorie in God, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=18}}† and knovvest his vvil, and approuest the more profitable things, instructed by the Lavv, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=19}}† presumest that thy self art a leader of the blinde, a light of them that are in darknes, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=20}}† a teacher of the folish, a maister of infants, hauing the forme of science & of veritie in the Lavv. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=21}}† Thou therfore {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is a shameful and damnable thing for preachers, teachers, or other guides of mens life, to commit the same things them selues which they reproue in other.}}∷ that teachest an other, teachest not thy self: that preachest, men ought not to steale, thou stealest: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=22}}† that saiest men should not commit aduoutrie, thou committest aduoutrie: that abhorrest idols, thou doest sacrilege: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=23}}† that doest glorie in the Lavv, thou by preuarication of the Lavv doest dishonour God. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=24}}† ({{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Es. 52, 5. Ez. 36, 20.''}}* ''For '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is a great sinne that by the il life of the faithful, our Lordes name should be il spoken of amōg the misbeleuers, & many withdrawen from the true religiō thereby. · Es. 52, 5. Ez. 36, 20.}}∷ ''the name of God through you is blasphemed among the Gentiles'', as it is vvriten.) {{verse|chapter=2|verse=25}}† Circumcision in deede profiteth, if thou obserue the Lavv: but if thou be a<noinclude>{{rh|||preuaricatour}}</noinclude>
